run.procedureSummary: 1. Load: add the cycle's input row to x, position by position, with no ceiling check. 2. Projection sweep (Gauss-Seidel): for i = 1 to 6 in order, if x_i > c_i, set x_i = c_i and add the excess to x_(i+1) before checking i+1, so excess can cascade. Excess from position 6 goes to slack. Only the ceiling is projected. 3. Active-set update on the swept x: an INACTIVE position with x_i >= u_i becomes ACTIVE; an ACTIVE position with x_i <= d_i becomes INACTIVE; otherwise the flag stays. Each change is logged as (cycle, position, before, after). 4. Jacobi transfer: first compute every amount from the same x (INACTIVE: floor(x_i/4); ACTIVE: floor(x_i/2)). Then subtract each amount from its own position, all at once. INACTIVE amounts go to slack. ACTIVE amounts go to position i-1, except position 1's, which goes to slack. No ceiling check. 5. Penalty reset: if sum(x) > 38 (strictly greater), set every x_i = floor(x_i/2), add the removed x_i - floor(x_i/2) to slack, and log the cycle. At 38 or below, do nothing. Report: end x, end flags, the flag-change log, the reset cycles, slack, and the balance check.

openPoints.point: How much a reset removes when x_i is odd
openPoints.assumption: The kept value is floor(x_i/2) and the removed part is x_i - floor(x_i/2) (that is, ceil(x_i/2)). All of the removed part goes to slack.

openPoints.point: Whether the loss tally is the same as the slack accumulator
openPoints.assumption: lossTotal is the final slack. Slack collects sweep excess from position 6, INACTIVE transfer amounts, position 1's ACTIVE transfer, and penalty-reset removals.
Step 4 uses the flags just set in step 3 of the same cycle.
The test is the plain sum of x after the transfer, slack not included, and it must be strictly above 38. In cycle 5 the sum is exactly 38, so no reset.

openPoints.point: Positions above their ceiling at the end of the run
openPoints.assumption: They are left as they are. Position 2 ends at 10 against a ceiling of 8, which the write-up allows after cycle 5.
